items.abstract: <jats:p>Economic fields commonly employ different objects, models, and local behavioral descriptions. This paper reconstructs the principal fields of a closed economy within one ordered axiomatic structure: rational expectations, maximin, certainty equivalent, transaction, and multiple roles. Agents form role-specific certainty equivalents from heterogeneous information, protect the weakest essential condition through a hierarchical choice correspondence, and alter those conditions through transactions that propagate across multiple roles. The essential set is agent-and role-specific rather than fixed. It is formed by accumulated assets, active roles, commitments, and inherited consumption or production structures; current income affects the feasibility of maintaining that set and may alter it indirectly by enabling changes in those structures. The framework thereby connects microeconomic choice, market participation, effective demand and supply, sustainable equilibrium, and endogenous economic cycles within one common structure.</jats:p>
title: A General Theory of Economics from Five Axioms

items.abstract: <jats:p>In this article, we consider the singular p-biharmonic problem involving Hardy potential and critical Hardy–Sobolev exponent. Firstly, we study the existence of ground state solutions by using the minimization method on the associated Nehari manifold. Then, we investigate the least-energy sign-changing solutions by considering the Nehari nodal set. In both cases, the critical Sobolev exponent is of great importance as the solutions exists only if we are below the critical Sobolev exponent.</jats:p>
title: Existence Results for Singular p-Biharmonic Problem with HARDY Potential and Critical Hardy-Sobolev Exponent
